Title: Diagnosis of test `testDefaultArgName`

Details:
- The test `testDefaultArgName` is creating an Option with `OptionBuilder.hasArg().isRequired().create("f")` and then adding it to Options.
- It sets a custom argument name "argument" in the HelpFormatter using `formatter.setArgName("argument")`.
- The test expects the usage string to include `-f <argument>` indicating that the argument name used in the usage string matches the one set in the HelpFormatter.

Investigation of the HelpFormatter code:
- The `HelpFormatter.printUsage` method constructs a usage string and for each option, it calls `appendOption()` to append the option syntax.
- In `appendOption()`, the code appends `-f` or `--longOpt` and if the option has an argument and has an argument name (`hasArgName()`), it appends `<argName>`.
- The `Option` class has a field `argName` and methods `getArgName()` (which returns this field) and `hasArgName()` (which checks if `argName` is non-null and non-empty).
- When `OptionBuilder.create("f")` is called, it creates an `Option` instance and sets its properties including `argName`.
- The `HelpFormatter` also has a method `setArgName(String name)` which sets `defaultArgName` in HelpFormatter, but this default argument name is never used in the `appendOption` method or anywhere in `printUsage`.

Conclusion:
The test expects that setting the argument name on the HelpFormatter via `formatter.setArgName("argument")` will change the argument name used in the usage output. However, the usage string output depends on the `argName` field in the `Option` instance itself, not on `HelpFormatter.defaultArgName`. Since the option created by `OptionBuilder` does not have the argument name "argument" set on it, the output does not reflect the default argument name from the HelpFormatter. The test fails because the formatter does not propagate the default argument name to the options it formats.

The root cause is that the `HelpFormatter.printUsage` and `appendOption` methods do not refer to or use the `defaultArgName` field of `HelpFormatter` when rendering the option usage description, causing the provided `argName` set on the formatter to have no effect.

---

Next, I would suggest checking how the `defaultArgName` set in `HelpFormatter` is supposed to be used and potentially fixing the `appendOption` method to use it when the option does not have its own argument name set.

The suspected code to fix is in: 
- `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.appendOption(StringBuffer, Option, boolean)`
- Possibly related: `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printUsage(PrintWriter, int, String, Options)`

Suggested methods to fix:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.appendOption(java.lang.StringBuffer,org.apache.commons.cli.Option,boolean)
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printUsage(java.io.PrintWriter,int,java.lang.String,org.apache.commons.cli.Options)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
